locked_by: agent via proposal P19, 2026-10-16, per sdd-kit-3 resolve-and-record

transport.harness_plane: Every tag outside category 'guest' is a substrate application event. The msgspec Struct class name equals the tag name, so the event kind on the run record IS the tag (substrate kernel/sequencer.py: event_kind = type(obj).__name__). Payload validation is the Struct's typed fields at the bus boundary.
transport.guest_plane: Category 'guest' tags are lines in a JSONL guest-trace file written by the profile under test (Windows reference tracer, VM guest runtime, native-process runtime). The file is content-addressed (trace_sha256) and ingested by the trace_ingester operator, which validates every line against this vocabulary and emits TRACE_INGESTED or TRACE_REJECTED on the harness plane. Guest lines never ride the substrate bus.
transport.ordering: Substrate seq orders orchestration work only (v0.2 section 11.4). Guest-trace order is the partial order given by (thread_id, thread_seq) plus hb_refs; substrate seq is never used to order guest effects.

types.id: string, ULID or stable slug; unique per entity kind
types.contract_id: string, dotted stable identifier, e.g. windows.event.auto_reset.single_signal
types.version: string, major.minor[.patch] (the vocabulary's own version is major.minor)
types.u64: integer >= 0; on the harness plane limited to [-(2^53-1), 2^53-1] because substrate canonicalizes payloads with RFC 8785 (larger values must be strings); the guest plane keeps the full 64-bit range
types.i64: integer; on the harness plane limited to [-(2^53-1), 2^53-1] because substrate canonicalizes payloads with RFC 8785 (larger values must be strings); the guest plane keeps the full 64-bit range
types.text: string, lowercase first word, no exclamation mark, no credential material

entities.name: Contract
entities.definition: A versioned, machine-readable behavioral definition with a stable identifier.

entities.name: Evidence
entities.definition: A documented requirement, an observed implementation behavior, or a hypothesis supporting a contract.

entities.name: ReferenceProfile
entities.definition: Windows build, CPU identity and features, library versions, GPU and driver, hashes, initial state, controlled inputs.

entities.name: DestinationProfile
entities.definition: The Mac host and backend capabilities a target run or artifact depends on.

entities.name: ApplicationProfile
entities.definition: A selected game's distribution, dependency graph, execution paths, graphics profile, and service requirements.

entities.name: Backend
entities.definition: Execution mode: native_process or managed_vm.

entities.name: Probe
entities.definition: A small discriminating program run to observe behavior.

entities.name: Execution
entities.definition: One run of a probe, application, or candidate runtime on one profile, producing a guest trace.

entities.name: Trace
entities.definition: The content-addressed guest-trace file of one execution.

entities.name: ModelCheck
entities.definition: Exploration of the executions a contract permits for one program.

entities.name: Comparison
entities.definition: Application of one declared relation between a reference and a target.

entities.name: Discrepancy
entities.definition: A failed comparison, minimized and classified.

entities.name: Candidate
entities.definition: An implementation candidate generated against an unchanged contract version.

entities.name: Translation
entities.definition: Native code for a guest address range at a code version, with its assumptions.

entities.name: Artifact
entities.definition: A generated output with source hashes, contract versions, compiler version, and evidence.

entities.name: Capability
entities.definition: An observed destination capability on a named host.

entities.name: Measurement
entities.definition: A performance number recorded apart from semantic acceptance.

entities.name: Distribution
entities.definition: The Windows depot content of one Steam app build.

entities.name: SteamSession
entities.definition: The launch/session state the application's Steamworks calls depend on.

entities.name: BridgeInterface
entities.definition: A versioned Windows-facing Steam interface and its Mac endpoint.

entities.name: Bundle
entities.definition: The native Mac application bundle produced for an application profile.

entities.name: GuestThread
entities.definition: A Windows-visible thread inside an execution; the unit of guest-trace ordering.

categories.name: contract
categories.description: Contract versions: proposed, accepted, revised, rejected, invalidation of dependents.

categories.name: probe
categories.description: Probe authorship, executions on profiles, trace ingest.

categories.name: verify
categories.description: Comparison, reduction, discrepancy report, routing, resolution.

categories.name: capability
categories.description: Destination capability probes and backend evaluation/selection.

categories.name: product
categories.description: Acquisition, Steam session and bridge, launch, lifecycle.

categories.name: guest
categories.description: Guest-trace lines from a profile under test.

tags.name: SESSION_INIT
tags.note: First application event of every w2m harness run (after substrate's own RunStarted). profile names the ReferenceProfile or DestinationProfile the run targets; contract_version names the contract-set version in force. Every later tag is read against this baseline.

tags.name: SESSION_COMPLETED
tags.note: Last application event of every harness run. accepted_count counts CONTRACT_ACCEPTED + CANDIDATE_ACCEPTED + ARTIFACT_ACCEPTED in this run; discrepancy_count counts DISCREPANCY_REPORTED.

tags.name: EVIDENCE_RECORDED
tags.note: One piece of evidence enters the record. source_ref is a URL plus retrieval date for documented, an execution_id for observed, a model_check_id or reasoning reference for hypothesis. applicability names the profiles it covers (e.g. 'windows_reference:win11-26100/x86-64'). distinguishing_check is required for hypothesis: the observation or model check that would separate it from alternatives.

tags.name: EVIDENCE_SUPERSEDED
tags.note: An evidence entry is replaced; the old entry stays on the record (no deletion).

tags.name: HYPOTHESIS_RESOLVED
tags.note: A hypothesis is settled by named observed or documented evidence. Repeated observations alone never resolve a hypothesis into a universal rule (v0.2 11.1).

tags.name: CONTRACT_PROPOSED
tags.note: A candidate behavioral definition is written to contracts/ and offered for model and reference checks.

tags.name: CONTRACT_ACCEPTED
tags.note: A contract version becomes an acceptance condition. Implementations are judged against exactly this (contract_id, version) until a CONTRACT_REVISED.

tags.name: CONTRACT_REVISED
tags.note: The contract-revision path (v0.2 11.3): a new accepted version replaces an old one on evidence. Always followed by DEPENDENTS_INVALIDATED for the same contract_id.

tags.name: CONTRACT_REJECTED
tags.note: A proposed version failed its model or reference checks and is not accepted.

tags.name: DEPENDENTS_INVALIDATED
tags.note: Everything that claimed conformance to from_version is marked for revalidation (v0.2 14). Counts are what was invalidated, not what was revalidated.

tags.name: PROBE_AUTHORED
tags.note: A probe program enters the content store. origin=reduced means a reducer produced it from parent_probe_id.

tags.name: EXECUTION_STARTED
tags.note: A program begins running on one named profile. injected_inputs_sha256 covers clock observations, input events, and service responses for controlled replay (v0.2 3.1). The timeout is per execution; there is no global constant. An execution imported from elsewhere (the Windows runner) omits what the harness did not set or observe and names each omitted or inferred field, with the reason, in unobserved (0.4, P13).

tags.name: EXECUTION_COMPLETED
tags.note: The program ended and its trace was collected. A guest fault is exit_status=faulted and is an observation, not a harness failure. timed_out means the harness killed it after timeout_seconds. exit_code and elapsed_seconds are omitted when not observed; unobserved says which and why (0.4, P13).

tags.name: EXECUTION_FAILED
tags.note: The harness could not obtain an execution: launch failed, the transport to the reference machine dropped, the profile did not match its declaration, or harness code raised. No trace exists; the execution is not evidence.

tags.name: TRACE_INGESTED
tags.note: Every line of the guest trace validated against this vocabulary (strict extras). Only an ingested trace may be cited as observed evidence or used in a comparison.

tags.name: TRACE_REJECTED
tags.note: A guest trace failed validation (unknown tag, missing field, extra field, broken thread_seq). The trace is kept but cannot be evidence.

tags.name: MODEL_CHECK_STARTED
tags.note: Exploration of the executions contract_version permits for one program begins, bounded at state_bound states.

tags.name: MODEL_CHECK_COMPLETED
tags.note: exhaustive=false means state_bound was hit; the permitted set is a lower bound and an outcome outside it is inconclusive, not forbidden.

tags.name: COMPARISON_COMPLETED
tags.note: One declared relation (v0.2 3) applied between a reference (an execution_id on a reference profile, or a model_check_id) and a target execution. rule_ref names the published rule for numerical_envelope. first_divergence is set when verdict=discrepancy: thread_id:thread_seq of the first diverging guest line, or the field path.

tags.name: REDUCTION_COMPLETED
tags.note: Delta-reduction of a failing program ended. If nothing could be removed, minimized equals source and steps=0. preserved_mismatch=false means the reduction lost the failure and the source program is reported instead.

tags.name: DISCREPANCY_REPORTED
tags.note: The v0.2 11.3 structured discrepancy: everything the generation system needs to reproduce the failure without prose. mismatch_class is the relation that failed.

tags.name: DISCREPANCY_ROUTED
tags.note: Deterministic routing: reference conforms to the contract and target does not -> implementation_repair; reference violates the contract -> contract_revision; otherwise undetermined, which needs a new probe.

tags.name: DISCREPANCY_RESOLVED
tags.note: resolving_ref is the CANDIDATE_ACCEPTED candidate_id, the CONTRACT_REVISED contract_id@to_version, or the decision that excluded the profile.

tags.name: CANDIDATE_GENERATED
tags.note: An implementation candidate is produced against an unchanged acceptance condition. generator_ref names the substrate topology and model (or 'hand'). discrepancy_id is set on a repair attempt.

tags.name: CANDIDATE_ACCEPTED
tags.note: Every cited comparison has verdict=conforms under this exact contract version. Measurements are never cited here (v0.2 3.1).

tags.name: CANDIDATE_REJECTED
tags.note: A candidate failed a check or altered its acceptance condition.

tags.name: ACCEPTANCE_CONDITION_ALTERED
tags.note: The acceptance guard found that a candidate changed an expected output, a checker, a contract, or evidence (v0.2 11.3: no candidate may change its expected output to pass). The guard is a separate operator from the generator. Forces CANDIDATE_REJECTED.

tags.name: CODE_TARGET_DISCOVERED
tags.note: A guest instruction target becomes known. Shipped code first reached at run time is discovery=runtime_transfer, stage=execution (v0.2 5.1). Discovery selects work; it does not define meaning.

tags.name: TRANSLATION_PUBLISHED
tags.note: Native code for [guest_range_start, guest_range_end) at code_version becomes enterable. AOT and on-demand translations carry the same fields and acceptance rules (v0.2 6).

tags.name: TRANSLATION_INVALIDATED
tags.note: A translation's assumptions no longer hold. After this, entering its range must resolve to a new translation or the prescribed fault.

tags.name: STALE_TRANSLATION_ENTERED
tags.note: Violation of the v0.2 5.1 execution invariant: an invalidated or wrong-version translation ran. Must never fire in an accepted build; fires only from a validity checker in test builds.

tags.name: ARTIFACT_BUILT
tags.note: A generated artifact is written with its v0.2 14 identity. source_sha256 is the hash over all input hashes.

tags.name: ARTIFACT_ACCEPTED
tags.note: The artifact passed every cited comparison and may be reused from cache under its validity conditions.

tags.name: ARTIFACT_INVALIDATED
tags.note: An artifact may no longer be reused; regeneration happens at the earliest valid stage.

tags.name: CAPABILITY_PROBED
tags.note: One destination capability observed on one host (v0.2 8.1). An observation about this development Mac is evidence for its profile only (v0.2 8.2). outcome=not_established: the probe could not decide; detail says what was searched or run (0.4, P12; v0.2 8.1 forbids asserting an absence the evidence does not show).

tags.name: BACKEND_EVALUATED
tags.note: One backend measured on one application path with its required host interfaces in place (v0.2 8.2, 13).

tags.name: BACKEND_SELECTED
tags.note: A recorded backend decision; decision_ref cites the BLACKBOARD Decisions entry. evaluation_ids cover both backends.

tags.name: MEASUREMENT_RECORDED
tags.note: A performance number, kept apart from semantic acceptance (v0.2 3.1). Quality settings are fixed by application_profile_id. variant names the configuration measured when one metric compares alternatives (e.g. 'ldapr_stlr', 'entso_on'). ns_per_access is wall-clock nanoseconds divided by guest memory accesses performed. vm_compile_blocks counts blocks the compiler in the VM handled, variant naming the outcome (compiled, or a refusal or cut cause, vm_backend.VMC_COUNT_NAMES).

tags.name: DISTRIBUTION_RESOLVED
tags.note: The Windows depots for one Steam app build are named. platform is 'windows' for every w2m input.

tags.name: DISTRIBUTION_ACQUIRED
tags.note: The depot content is on disk under the user's account. content_sha256 hashes the sorted file manifest.

tags.name: ACQUISITION_FAILED
tags.note: Acquisition stopped. auth_required means a real account step is pending; the system never fabricates success (v0.2 4.1).

tags.name: APPLICATION_PREPARED
tags.note: The bundle exists and its manifest names the backend used (v0.2 4.3, 14).

tags.name: STEAM_SESSION_ESTABLISHED
tags.note: The application's Steamworks initialization succeeded through the bridge against the real Mac Steam client.

tags.name: STEAM_SESSION_FAILED
tags.note: Steamworks initialization did not succeed; diagnostic names the failing interface call.

tags.name: BRIDGE_CALL_UNMAPPED
tags.note: A Windows-facing Steam interface method was called that has no Mac endpoint mapping (v0.2 4.2, 15). The fields are the diagnostic.

tags.name: APPLICATION_LAUNCHED
tags.note: The bundle's launcher started the application. A local executable launch and a Steam launch are distinguished by whether STEAM_SESSION_ESTABLISHED preceded it in the lifecycle.

tags.name: APPLICATION_EXITED
tags.note: The application process (or guest) ended.

tags.name: SAVE_STATE_VERIFIED
tags.note: Saved state written in one launch was read back in the next and matched under the storage contract.

tags.name: APPLICATION_UPDATED
tags.note: A new build replaced the old one; affected artifacts were invalidated and state preserved.

tags.name: APPLICATION_REMOVED
tags.note: The application and its generated artifacts were removed from the command line.

tags.name: PRODUCT_LIFECYCLE_QUALIFIED
tags.note: One product-slice qualification result. profile_scope states the covered categories (v0.2 12.1: every qualification result states its profile).

tags.name: GUEST_TRACE_OPENED
tags.note: First line of every guest-trace file; the SESSION_INIT of the guest plane.

tags.name: GUEST_THREAD_STARTED
tags.note: A guest thread exists. thread_seq is 0. hb_refs holds the creating thread's 'thread_id:thread_seq'.

tags.name: GUEST_THREAD_EXITED
tags.note: A guest thread terminated; its thread object becomes signaled (v0.2 7).

tags.name: GUEST_CALL_RETURNED
tags.note: An observed API boundary call returned. api is 'module!Function' (e.g. 'kernel32!WaitForSingleObject'). hb_refs carries the synchronizing edge, e.g. the SetEvent that satisfied a wait. args_sha256 is the sha256 of the UTF-8 canonical argument rendering 'Function(a1,a2,...)': handles and pointers by role name (e.g. 'event'), integers in decimal, no spaces (0.4 note; the tag's schema is unchanged).

tags.name: GUEST_MEMORY_OBSERVED
tags.note: An instrumented memory access in a probe (litmus tests, page-protection probes). Not emitted for every access in application runs.

tags.name: GUEST_FAULT_RAISED
tags.note: A guest-visible exception was raised (e.g. 0xC0000005 access violation, 0x80000001 guard page). Prescribed faults are observations, not failures.

tags.name: GUEST_CALLBACK_ENTERED
tags.note: Control entered guest code from the system side: window procedure, APC, thread-pool work, TLS callback, completion routine.

tags.name: GUEST_CLOCK_READ
tags.note: A clock observation (v0.2 3.1). Each clock has its own contract; tick_count wraps at 2^32 ms (about 49.7 days), so no universal monotonic check applies.

tags.name: GUEST_THREAD_STATE_OBSERVED
tags.note: The observing thread (thread_id) read another thread's scheduler state. thread_state and wait_reason are the operating system's raw values (Windows: SYSTEM_THREAD_INFORMATION.ThreadState and WaitReason from NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessInformation); documented meanings in .NET System.Diagnostics.ThreadState, Wait = 5, and ThreadWaitReason, UserRequest = 6, valid only when the state is Wait). source names the interface read. Used to witness a contract precondition such as 'both waiters are pending' (0.5, P14).

tags.name: GUEST_TRACE_CLOSED
tags.note: Last line of every guest-trace file. dropped_count > 0 means the tracer lost lines; such a trace is ingested but cannot support an exact or partial_order comparison.

tags.name: SERVICE_UNIMPLEMENTED
tags.note: A destination execution stopped because the guest called a Windows service ("DLL!Function", or an argument form of one) that w2m does not implement. Closes the execution like EXECUTION_COMPLETED; it is the frontier's measurement of what the application needs next (roadmap Sprint 038), not a guest fault and not a harness failure. guest_address is the call's return address in the guest. Distinct from BRIDGE_CALL_UNMAPPED, which is a Steam interface method with no Mac mapping (v0.2 4.2).

invariants.rule: SESSION_INIT is the first application event of a harness run.
SESSION_COMPLETED is the last application event of a harness run.

For each execution_id, exactly one EXECUTION_COMPLETED or EXECUTION_FAILED follows within timeout_seconds + kill_grace_seconds of EXECUTION_STARTED, measured on the harness clock. Not checked for an execution whose EXECUTION_STARTED omits timeout_seconds (an imported execution; 0.4, P13); its unobserved field says so.
invariants.source: v0.2 3.1 (timeouts are observable and cannot be erased)

invariants.rule: Each EXECUTION_COMPLETED is followed by exactly one TRACE_INGESTED or TRACE_REJECTED with the same trace_sha256 before SESSION_COMPLETED.
Line 1 of every guest trace is GUEST_TRACE_OPENED; the last line is GUEST_TRACE_CLOSED.
Within one trace, thread_seq for a given thread_id starts at 0 on GUEST_THREAD_STARTED and increases by exactly 1 per line; a gap is a validation failure (TRACE_REJECTED).
invariants.source: v0.2 9, 11.4 (guest order is per-thread plus hb edges)

invariants.rule: Every CONTRACT_REVISED is followed by DEPENDENTS_INVALIDATED for the same contract_id and to_version before SESSION_COMPLETED.

rules.rule: A version is accepted or rejected only after it was proposed.
Nothing may claim acceptance under a replaced version (v0.2 14).

payload_match: every comparison_ids entry has verdict=conforms and the same contract_version
rules.rule: Acceptance cites only conforming comparisons that precede it.
Reduction runs only on a discrepancy comparison.
Routing follows the report; resolution follows routing.

payload_match: discrepancy_id; repair_path=implementation_repair requires resolution=implementation_repaired, repair_path=contract_revision requires resolution=contract_revised
rules.rule: The repair path taken matches the route (v0.2 11.3 keeps the paths distinct).
An altered acceptance condition rejects the candidate; no CANDIDATE_ACCEPTED for it may follow.
Entering an invalidated translation is the incident the validity checker exists to catch; in an accepted build it never fires.

payload_match: application_profile_id; evaluation_ids include one native_process and one managed_vm evaluation
rules.rule: Backend selection follows evaluation of both candidates (v0.2 8.2).
Product lifecycle order: resolve, acquire, prepare, session, launch, exit, state verify, relaunch, update, remove, qualify.
Every launch ends in exactly one exit before the next launch of the same profile.

payload_match: application_profile_id; passed=true requires every lifecycle_step in steps_passed and a preceding event for each step
rules.rule: A passed qualification is backed by the whole lifecycle on the record.
Nothing follows GUEST_TRACE_CLOSED in a trace file.

operators.name: contract_builder
operators.model_route: substrate Responder for drafting contract text; acceptance is deterministic (checks pass) never model-judged
operators.fallback: hand authoring in a sprint, generator_ref='hand'

operators.name: probe_author
operators.model_route: substrate Responder for generated probes; origin field says which

operators.name: reference_runner
operators.runs_on: Windows reference machine (profile_kind windows_reference); tracer writes the guest plane

operators.name: destination_runner
operators.runs_on: this Mac, profile_kind native_process or managed_vm; the guest runtime writes the guest plane

operators.name: application_compiler
operators.runs_on: host at install/update; runtime component at execution

operators.name: product_driver
operators.runs_on: this Mac (the w2m CLI and launcher)

constraints.spec: observed: an execution_id with TRACE_INGESTED on record; documented: a URL and retrieval date; hypothesis: a model_check_id or a reasoning reference

constraints.target: EVIDENCE_RECORDED (observed) for contracts on instruction, ordering, or fault behavior
constraints.spec: the execution's profile_kind is windows_reference; windows_arm_emulated never satisfies it (v0.2 11.1)
required when relation=numerical_envelope; names a published rule (e.g. Direct3D 11 floating-point rules), never a tolerance chosen after the mismatch (v0.2 10.2)

CONTRACT_REJECTED.reason, EXECUTION_FAILED.diagnostic, TRACE_REJECTED.reason + first_invalid_line, DISCREPANCY_REPORTED.first_divergence + minimized_program_sha256, ACCEPTANCE_CONDITION_ALTERED.path + both hashes, STALE_TRANSLATION_ENTERED both code versions, ACQUISITION_FAILED.diagnostic, STEAM_SESSION_FAILED.diagnostic, BRIDGE_CALL_UNMAPPED interface_name + interface_version + method: non-empty

SESSION_COMPLETED.outcome, DEPENDENTS_INVALIDATED counts, EXECUTION_COMPLETED.exit_status, TRACE_INGESTED.line_count, MODEL_CHECK_COMPLETED.exhaustive, COMPARISON_COMPLETED.verdict, REDUCTION_COMPLETED.preserved_mismatch, BACKEND_EVALUATED counts, DISTRIBUTION_ACQUIRED.bytes, APPLICATION_PREPARED.artifact_count, PRODUCT_LIFECYCLE_QUALIFIED.passed, GUEST_TRACE_CLOSED.dropped_count: present, SERVICE_UNIMPLEMENTED.service (the service the run needs next).
never cite a measurement_id; performance is not acceptance (v0.2 3.1)
contains no password, Steam login token, 2FA code, or session key; scanned for credential patterns before append (v0.2 4.1: credentials are real service inputs, never record content)
lowercase first word, no exclamation mark, no emoji, absolute paths (WORKING_AGREEMENT.md tone canon)
resolves to an earlier event introducing that id in the same record, or to a registry file (profiles/, contracts/)

report_binding.guest_plane: Guest traces are cited by trace_sha256 in OBSERVED; first_divergence lines are quoted in DELTA.

project_overrides: Validator-extras posture: strict on both planes (msgspec forbid_unknown_fields on guest-trace ingest; Struct fields on the harness plane).
Adding an enum value is a PAYLOAD_FIELD_PROPOSED-class change and bumps the minor version, because a guest trace or record written with the new value would fail validation under the old version.

Guest-plane compatibility: a vocabulary version lists the earlier versions whose guest traces it still ingests (guest_plane_compatible_versions). A change to any guest tag removes earlier versions from the list.
